source.title: Opening the Black Box of Deep Neural Networks via Information

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes information flow and generalization during training on the task’s true labels. It does not test random labels, unstructured inputs, or the other listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation only while citing Zhang et al. (2016); it reports no result of its own on random-label fitting or those regularizers. Its own results on true-label information and generalization are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures information-plane dynamics on structured, rule-generated labels. It neither randomizes labels nor compares learning real patterns with memorizing noise. Its unregularized experiments lack a regularizer-removal comparison, so they do not establish V5's claim about the effect of removing regularization. Zhang et al. is cited as context.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors report an early fitting phase followed by longer compression, argue that SGD noise produces efficient representations near the information-bottleneck bound, and attribute computational benefits to depth. They condition their broader explanation of deep learning on these findings generalizing. They also report similar dynamics for a committee-machine rule and a diffusion transition on MNIST.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes information-plane trajectories and stochastic-gradient phases on synthetic rule-learning tasks; it does not apply the original random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different label-information trajectories for small and large training samples, and different training times with different numbers of hidden layers.

fits_no_version.finding: With 80% of rule-generated patterns, six hidden layers reached full relevant output information within 400 epochs; one hidden layer did not reach good label information after 10,000 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional hidden layers accelerate attainment of good output label information on this synthetic rule-learning task.

fits_no_version.finding: Compression reduced label information with 5% training samples, whereas label information mostly increased with 85% training samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of representation compression on generalization depends on training sample size.

record.problems: The tasks use synthetic binary rules with 12 binary inputs. The authors say direct information-plane estimation for large problems is beyond the scope of the work and that the findings should be verified on larger problems. The claim versions’ random-label and unstructured-input settings are not tested.
record.rows_left_out: No other own results were extracted: the paper’s remaining reported findings concern gradient statistics, information-bottleneck optimality, or other analyses that do not bear on the listed claim versions or the fitted-label generalization findings recorded here.

untested.parts: Completely random-label fitting, training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time for true versus random labels and convergence across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and test-error degradation across increasing random-label corruption.

Random-label fitting with regularizers and the effect of removing regularizers on true-label generalization. Good generalization without explicit regularization is reported, but no removal comparison is performed.
The relative timing of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The phrase random labeled samples in Section 3.4 refers to samples drawn from the structured rule in Eq. (10), not independently randomized labels. Fitting followed by compression is not evidence of real-label learning followed by noise memorization.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, chance test error, and whether architecture or training hyperparameters must change.
Training-time comparison for true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled, permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep from clean to fully corrupted labels.
The study does not test whether these regularizers affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
The study does not compare when real patterns and noisy or random labels are learned.

rows.subject: DNNs with 1 hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on 80% of patterns sampled from the study’s rule; information-plane trajectories averaged over randomized networks.
rows.measure: I(T;Y), described as corresponding to test or generalization error
rows.value: The network was unable to achieve good IY values even after 104 epochs.
rows.note: The result concerns the study’s true-label rule, not random-label fitting. The text reports an average over 50 randomized initial weights and training samples.
rows.check: The epoch count rendered as 104 means 10^4 (10,000) epochs. This measures output label information on a structured task, not random-label fitting.

rows.subject: DNNs with 6 hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Trained on 80% of patterns sampled from the study’s rule; information-plane trajectories averaged over randomized networks.
rows.measure: I(T;Y), described as corresponding to test or generalization error
rows.value: It reached the full relevant information at the output layer within 400 epochs.
rows.note: The result concerns the study’s true-label rule, not random-label fitting. The text reports an average over 50 randomized initial weights and training samples.
rows.check: The result is correctly summarized, but good label information without explicit regularization does not measure the effect of removing regularizers.

rows.subject: DNNs with up to 7 fully connected hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared information-plane trajectories for networks trained on different proportions of patterns sampled from the study’s rule.
rows.measure: I(T;Y), described as corresponding to test or generalization error
rows.value: The compression phase significantly reduced the layers’ label information.
rows.note: The text says the trajectories were averaged over networks and describes the result for the small-sample case; it does not report a numerical error rate.
rows.check: Figure 3 specifies five hidden layers with widths 10, 8, 6, 4 and 2, rather than an unspecified network with up to seven hidden layers. The condition varies sample size, not label corruption.

rows.subject: DNNs with up to 7 fully connected hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared information-plane trajectories for networks trained on different proportions of patterns sampled from the study’s rule.
rows.measure: I(T;Y), described as corresponding to test or generalization error
rows.value: The label information mostly increased during the compression phase.
rows.note: The text describes the large-sample case; it does not report a numerical error rate.
rows.check: Figure 3 specifies five hidden layers with widths 10, 8, 6, 4 and 2. The increase concerns information about the underlying rule, not fitting randomly corrupted labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
